name: Aleut (Unangax̂)

scope: Bounded independent evidence/schema review. No canonical or Site edits and no broad source discovery. Existing named originals were spot-checked as recorded; this is not a second full inspection of every work.

sourceCountAssessment.supportingCards: Archive finding aid plus retained APIA Tribes directory. The latter must explicitly remain outside the substantive minimum.

materialFindings.finding: Section 207's principal compensation-in-lieu provision also has a limited village site surface-estate conveyance authorization in subsection (e), continuing onto102 Stat. 916. A categorical no-conveyance account would omit that exception.
materialFindings.preciseCorrection: Title II addressed Attu land losses principally through compensation while also authorizing limited site conveyances. This did not mean restoration of Attu village. Describe statutory authorization, not proof of implementation.
materialFindings.scopeCorrection: Visible law scope should include102 Stat. 903–904 and911–916; independent additional inspection of the continuation is recorded below.
clarifications: The named recipient is the statute's defined Corporation, the Aleut Corporation, not every tribal government.
Subsection(e) concerns the traditional village surface estate and surrounding parcel. My initial message's cemetery shorthand was corrected after reading916 and must not enter the profile.

materialFindings.finding: The actual pages label2025-02-19 and2024-10-16 as Last updated, not verified original publication dates.
materialFindings.preciseCorrection: Use updatedAt or documentDate stating Last updated; do not call these original publication dates.

claimFitAssessment.history: No substantive mismatch found between the proposed wartime claims and checked NPS/memoir texts. Attuan captivity in Japan remains distinct from U.S.-administered Southeast Alaska camps. Survivor statements are attributed; casualty totals, exact duration and every-person compensation claims are omitted.
claimFitAssessment.community: No incorrect government equivalence found. APIA is a regional nonprofit; Aleut Corporation is a shareholder business; Qawalangin and St. Paul are particular governments. The constitutional account is tied to its1997 adoption, program schedules and contamination-record date discrepancies remain qualified, and newsletter priorities are dated rather than current outcome claims.
claimFitAssessment.language: Direct UAF read supports Unangam Tunuu naming, Eastern/Western plural forms and collaborative work with named speakers. Population/speaker estimates and linked tools are explicitly outside the claim. Alutiiq/Sugpiaq is correctly kept distinct.
claimFitAssessment.countAndUse: Every packet source is used meaningfully in its proposed prose. No unread film, book catalogue, archive item, nominee sanctuary document or same-work mirror is added to the substantive count.
